title: MVVM and Other App Architecture Patterns knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the most direct learning goal for this lesson?
options: Use mvvm and other app architecture patterns only for visual styling.
Skip type checking and accept any result.
Replace a focused example with unrelated code.
The main goal is to apply model-view-viewmodel in a small Swift example and verify the result.
questions.answer_key: The main goal is to apply model-view-viewmodel in a small Swift example and verify the result.
questions.explanation: MVVM and Other App Architecture Patterns is best learned through a small, verifiable example. SwiftUI describes the interface as a hierarchy of views derived from state. Keep state ownership clear, compose reusable views, and verify keyboard, accessibility, and size-adaptation behavior.

questions.prompt: Which practice supports maintainable Swift code?
options: Ignore ownership and errors when an example works once.
Use the newest API without checking target compatibility.
Use documented Swift semantics, explicit data flow and a test for a meaningful edge case.
Force all values through unsafe operations.
questions.answer_key: Use documented Swift semantics, explicit data flow and a test for a meaningful edge case.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification step for a code example?
options: Test only the happy path and skip environment details.
Compile/run in the intended environment and confirm behavior against the versioned reference.
Rely on a source screenshot without running or inspecting it.
Assume the browser preview compiled Swift successfully.
questions.answer_key: Compile/run in the intended environment and confirm behavior against the versioned reference.
